PullRequest.Title: simplify customization hint
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each eligible chat request recomputed disabled MCP migration support by creating a short-lived scope, waiting for its debounced all-server assessment, and disposing it, preventing reuse and delaying agent invocation even though the feature was disabled.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: At least the scope's 50 ms debounce plus MCP support assessment time was added to eligible chat-request preparation whenever migration hints were enabled while the default-disabled MCP migration remained off.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: computeMigrationHint now checks the MCP migration enablement before scheduling its four-way Promise.all and substitutes an already-resolved empty migration when disabled, removing fresh support-scope creation and the 50 ms debounced MCP assessment from the chat request critical path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 73 unconditionally included computeMigration(...McpServers) in computeMigrationHint's Promise.all. ChatService calls computeMigrationHint while collecting every eligible request's context and awaits that Promise.all before preparing variables and invoking the agent (chatServiceImpl.ts:1681-1695,1773-1778). The MCP provider acquires a support scope and awaits waitForMcpServerSupport (agentHostMcpServerMigrationProvider.ts:52-60); a newly acquired scope schedules support assessment behind MCP_SUPPORT_UPDATE_DEBOUNCE_DELAY = 50 and is disposed when the call returns (agentHostMcpServerSupportScope.ts:22,155-215,269-273). MCP migration defaults to false (chat.shared.contribution.ts:2528-2534), and provider-side disabling only skipped createPlan after support resolution, so the old hint path still paid scope creation, debounce, and all-server support assessment despite producing no MCP candidates. The added conditional at line 105 bypasses the provider entirely in that default-disabled case.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sending an Agent Host chat request while customization migration hints are enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatService awaits hook collection, automatic instructions, and computeMigrationHint together before preparing variables and invoking the agent. The changed MCP-enable check is therefore on the request critical path; when MCP migration is disabled it now resolves locally instead of awaiting MCP support. Hint rendering occurs later and is trivial local work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover user/local prompt, agent, instruction, and skill files used to form file migration candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold hint computation requests agent and instructions from two migration branches plus prompt and skill once; established per-type promise caches coalesce/reuse discovery when their locator event is active, while invalidation follows file/plugin change events. Candidate aggregation remains in-memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same three file migration computations and prompt discovery calls were already part of hint computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These discoveries are awaited by computeMigrationHint before the chat request can proceed to agent invocation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and settle an MCP support assessment after a 50 ms debounce, reading all current server definitions and waiting for initial local MCP-server loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one support-scope assessment per MCP hint computation when no compatible scope is already retained; a zero-ref scope is disposed, so subsequent Always-mode requests can be cold again.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, hint computation entered this boundary even though MCP migration defaults to disabled; the diff removes that work in the disabled case.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When MCP migration is enabled, computeMigration awaits support settlement. When disabled, the added gate removes this boundary from the request critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse eligible workspace .vscode/mcp.json files while creating MCP migration candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per distinct eligible source URI due to ResourceMap memoization, even when several servers share a file; zero when MCP migration is disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Enabled planning had the same grouped reads; disabled planning already skipped file reads, but still paid support-scope settlement until this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Enabled MCP migration planning is awaited by the hint; disabled migration now bypasses planning and support acquisition entirely.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of discovered customization files, distinct prompt types/source locations, MCP servers, and distinct eligible workspace MCP configuration files; in Always hint mode the scenario repeats per chat request, while Once mode records state after the first shown hint.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The three file migration computations and optional MCP computation run concurrently in one Promise.all. Each file migration's source-folder types are handled sequentially, while prompt discovery may coalesce through cachedFileLocations promises. MCP planning iterates servers sequentially and memoizes source reads by source URI, so effective filesystem cardinality is per distinct eligible workspace MCP file, not per server.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt file lists use per-type promise caches invalidated by locator/plugin updates. MCP source-file reads are coalesced only within one plan by source URI. MCP support scopes are refcounted and removed at zero references, so an unshared hint computation is cold; the new disabled-feature gate avoids that cache lifecycle entirely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the awaited chat call path, default-disabled setting, support-scope debounce/lifecycle, grouped file reads, and new bypass are all explicit in code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact prompt/MCP inventory and whether the migration-hint experiment selects Once or Always vary by user. The removed support path has a code-defined 50 ms debounce before assessment, while additional assessment duration is environment-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No diff-introduced regression. The change removes repeated MCP support work from the default-disabled critical path; enabled behavior preserves existing boundary cardinality. New Map/filter aggregation is transient O(servers + candidates) work over already-materialized arrays and does not materially amplify cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Computing or displaying MCP migrations in the Chat Customizations management flow
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Direct MCP migration computation still acquires and settles the support scope and, when enabled, builds a plan before the management UI receives the result. Adding storage provenance happens after the settled snapshot is available and before return.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read eligible workspace MCP configuration files to validate migration candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per distinct eligible .vscode/mcp.json source URI, grouped across servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical reads and grouping occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for enabled migration planning before results are shown; storage classification adds no boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assess all known MCP servers and wait for initial local MCP-server discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One assessment per scope update, shared while scope references remain alive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The management flow already required the same support snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The provider waits for a settled snapshot before returning management data.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total known MCP servers and distinct eligible workspace MCP source files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Support assessment is debounced/coalesced inside one retained scope. Candidate planning is sequential over servers, with one memoized read per distinct source file. The added source-kind switch runs once per in-scope server with no asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The support scope is reused by normalized session/root key while retained and invalidated by MCP/configuration changes. Plan file reads are memoized only within a computation; no cache semantics changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added operation is a constant-time enum switch during the existing per-server projection and does not cross a boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Server counts and scope retention depend on workspace and whether the management UI remains open.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds one small storage field and O(1) classification per existing result item, with unchanged support assessment, I/O cardinality, and concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering customization migration hint text and action links in a chat response
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After request context is collected and the agent path is established, ChatService constructs two command-link strings and a MarkdownString synchronously before reporting progress.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed-size hint and two links per shown request; message text no longer scales with multiple separate hint fragments.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous rendering step per shown hint; Once mode suppresses later hints in the session, Always mode can render once per request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Shown state is stored in the chat input model for Once mode and workspace storage handles explicit dismissal; the changed labels do not alter either lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines only replace localized strings and tooltips.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Only the configured hint mode controls frequency; payload size is fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; no DOM/layout, IPC, filesystem, subprocess, database, or network work is introduced by the text changes.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages. No actionable performance regression was introduced. Recorded the new MCP-enable gate as a high-confidence fix for repeated default-disabled MCP support assessment on the chat request critical path.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
